summary: 120-foot steel fire tower in Worcester County, Maryland, built 1928-29 by a woodland owners' association; cab removed or replaced around 1996, sources differ; now a state communications site.

facts.status_note: Standing. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks it as having no cab; the state report says the cab was replaced with a wooden deck.

access.note: Sits on a Maryland DNR Forest Service field office and communications compound fronting Snow Hill Road. No source says the public may visit or climb it.

events.note: Register and state tower report date installation to 1929; a 1928 newspaper and a 1929 state report describe construction in fall 1928
Deputy Warden Samuel Long named as watchman at the tower in October 1929
District forester said only one forest fire had been reported from the tower since its erection
Margie Smullin Dennis in charge; the paper called her the only woman fire tower warden on the Eastern Shore
Stairs replaced; the Register says the cab was removed, the state report says it was replaced with a wooden deck

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1928 newspaper and a 1929 state report describe construction in fall 1928; the Register and the state tower report give 1929 for installation. The story reports both dates.

The Register says the cab was removed in 1996; the state report says it was replaced with a wooden deck; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower as standing without its cab. The story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Brief status_note matches the FFLA list but omits the state report's wooden-deck account. A 1929 Forest Worker item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page places a 120-foot tower at Millville, Worcester County; not reconciled and not used. No visiting information found, so access is set to restricted. No photos added.
